purpose: Produce a source-bounded design-map manuscript that consolidates machine-verifiable scientific records and plural review governance without claiming empirical superiority.
audience: Scholarly communication, computational science, research infrastructure, metascience, and governance researchers; private internal review at this stage.
outline: Motivate the gap between cosmetic rerendering and scientific review.
Define epistemic achievement separately from record, resources, and governance.
Map representative prior systems and standards as components to reuse.
Specify shared claim/evidence records and plural trust-domain views.
Apply the design to portable and HPC/restricted workflows.
State threat boundaries, falsifiers, limitations, and first unmet gates.
retrieval_capability: bounded local evidence corpus plus citation identity tools; no independent exhaustive corpus search performed in this drafting pass
figures_tables: No external figures in this draft
human_questions: Who accepts authorship responsibility and approves AI-assistance disclosure?
Which exact venue and article type should govern final length and style?
Which public or sanitized HPC workflow can support the second case without exposing restricted material?
What evidence would justify promoting the plural-trust architecture from design profile to empirical recommendation?
constraints: Private draft; no submission, preprint, public release, or external contact.
Contribution posture is synthesis, unification, clarification, and operational consolidation.
No mock results, invented citations, privacy guarantees, or machine-validity claims.
Every assessment mode must state exclusions and resource burden.
R0 is the portable floor for lightweight work, not a universal gate for expensive science.
excluded_claims: Plural trust views outperform global reputation.
The worked cases have been implemented or independently reviewed.
This is the first system to combine provenance, review, and reputation.
